NostrEventsTests: C# signatures byte-identical to the Python reference for every vector; flipped id, flipped sig bits, tampered content/created_at/kind/tag/pubkey, 31/33/0-byte and off-curve pubkey, uppercase hex and relay junk all fail Verify without throwing. acceptance: Export, wipe storage, import: the games list rebuilds from relays and play continues
Failure: importing an invalid or short key is rejected with a message and the existing key is not replaced
Wording of the warning is reviewed by the copy lens (Q-017 decides the UX before build)

features.behaviour: Resign: either player can resign at any time; the opponent's client ends the game as won
acceptance: Resign with confirmation on my turn and on the opponent's turn: both clients show the result
Cancel at the confirmation sends nothing
Edge: a resign sent while the opponent's move was in flight still ends the game on both sides; a move arriving after a resign is ignored
Failure: a RESIGN from a stranger key or for another game is dropped; a resign that no relay accepts stays 'pending delivery' and retries

features.behaviour: Opponent-offline status: 'waiting for opponent, last move seen <time>' and an outbox banner when I am offline
acceptance: Opponent idle 10+ minutes on their turn: the waiting line shows the last verified opponent event time
Own network off: banner says moves are queued; a move made offline is sent when the network returns
Failure: no automatic forfeit appears before Day 7 under any condition

features.behaviour: Day-7 auto-draw is agreed between clients (signed timeout notice) rather than unilateral, per the design accepted in M5
acceptance: Both clients online past Day 7 end the game as a draw with the same final result
Failure: a timeout notice from a client whose clock says Day 6 is not applied by the other; disagreement is shown as 'opponent says timed out, you disagree' and the game stays open

features.behaviour: Desktop multiplayer: Avalonia desktop hosts or joins an invite over relays through the coordinator, plays, resumes and shows rejected moves
acceptance: Desktop on Windows vs browser (or CLI) on another machine: 5x5 game to a road win with equal hash
Close and reopen the desktop app mid-game: the game resumes
Failure: a bad invite shows the invite-spec message; a forged move from the test-peer tool shows the rejected-move banner

features.behaviour: Repository is honest to a newcomer: LICENSE file exists (Q-014) and the README device matrix matches features.json
acceptance: LICENSE present and matches what the README badge says
README 'Implemented' column equals the v1 platform set (Web, CLI, Windows desktop) and marks Android as experimental, iOS/macOS as not in v1 (D-018)
Failure: a grep for the removed claims (PWA, drag-and-drop, 114/107 tests) in README finds none

features.behaviour: Key-storage threat model is written and the cheap mitigations are in: where the secret lives per head, what an XSS or a shared device exposes, what export does
acceptance: A one-page threat model exists under docs/decisions/ or pipeline/ and names the browser storage choice and why
Security lens review pass finds no secret in logs, URLs or analytics on any head
Failure: the invite link and the status lines never contain the secret key (grep + manual check)

features.behaviour: Release-binary run: the published CLI and desktop archives (not `dotnet run`) play a game to a road win over relays
acceptance: Download the release archives from GitHub, run CLI vs the Pages site, to a road win, equal hash
